spax: spatial accessibility and allocation modeling

spax models spatial access to services such as GP practices, and estimates how quickly the pull of a facility falls with travel time from where people actually go. Its allocation model is fitted to observed use (area-to-facility flows or facility totals), so the decay is estimated rather than assumed. The same inputs, decay curves and numeric engine compute floating catchment area (FCA) accessibility indices: 2SFCA, E2SFCA, M2SFCA, 3SFCA and Huff-2SFCA. Decay curves plug in: write your own as an R function and use it in an index or a fitted model.

The spax() interface and the allocation model are experimental and may change in later versions, while the one-call FCA functions spax_2sfca(), spax_e2sfca() and spax_m2sfca() are stable.

Install

Use R 4.4.0 or newer. This is the supported dependency and testing floor for spax 0.7.0.

Install the released version from CRAN, or version 0.7.0 by its release tag rather than from the repository’s default branch:

install.packages("spax")

# or from GitHub
# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("Songyosr/spax@v0.7.0")

Development continues on the develop branch (pak::pak("Songyosr/spax@develop")).

Each release is archived on Zenodo; doi:10.5281/zenodo.23438611 refers to all versions (version 0.6.0 is doi:10.5281/zenodo.23538560). Cite the version you used with citation("spax").

A first look

spax ships open data for GP care in Cornwall, in south-west England. This example computes the enhanced two-step FCA index (E2SFCA) for mainland Cornwall from a population grid, the GP practices with their GP full-time equivalents (FTE) and travel minutes from every grid cell to every practice.

library(spax)
library(terra)
library(sf)
library(dplyr)

gp <- cornwall_gp |>
  filter(!scilly) |>
  st_drop_geometry()
pop <- read_spax_example("cornwall_pop.tif")
travel_grid <- read_spax_example("cornwall_gp_travel.tif")[[gp$practice]]
# Keep cells with a travel time to every mainland practice
pop <- trim(mask(pop, sum(travel_grid)))
travel_grid <- crop(travel_grid, pop)
grid_data <- prep_data(pop, gp, travel_grid, id_col = "practice", supply_cols = "gp_fte_extg")

# The E2SFCA index with a Gaussian decay of travel scale 10 minutes
fca <- spax(grid_data, spec_e2sfca(decay = decay_gaussian(sigma = 10)))

# Mainland Cornwall's outline, in the grid's longitude and latitude
outline <- cornwall_lsoa |>
  filter(!scilly) |>
  st_union() |>
  vect()

plot(
  1000 * fca$accessibility,
  axes = FALSE,
  col = hcl.colors(50, "viridis"),
  main = "E2SFCA index, GP FTE per 1,000 residents"
)
lines(outline, lwd = 0.6)

The index is GP supply per resident, counting nearby practices more than distant ones. It is highest in the bright band between Redruth, Truro and Falmouth, below and left of center. It is lowest on Bodmin Moor, the dark patch above and right of center, and at the tips of the Land’s End (far left) and Lizard (bottom) peninsulas.

A fitted model

The allocation model describes where the residents of each small area register. Each practice attracts residents in proportion to its GP FTE, discounted by travel time, and an outside option takes the residents registered with a practice outside mainland Cornwall. spec_clm() specifies this model, a conditional logit model (CLM) with an outside option. By default it estimates two numbers: the travel scale σ of a Gaussian decay, which sets how fast a practice’s pull falls with travel time, and the outside weight v0. Here they are fitted to the registrations of each small area at each practice.

areas <- cornwall_lsoa |>
  filter(!scilly) |>
  st_drop_geometry()
gp <- cornwall_gp |>
  filter(!scilly) |>
  st_drop_geometry()
travel <- cornwall_travel[areas$lsoa, gp$practice]
demand <- setNames(areas$registered, areas$lsoa)
supply <- setNames(gp$gp_fte_extg, gp$practice)
d <- prep_data(demand, supply, travel, metadata = list(
  demand_units = "registered residents", demand_period = "July 2026",
  supply_units = "GP FTE excluding GPs in training", supply_period = "June 2026",
  travel_units = "minutes"))
flows <- obs_flows(cornwall_flows, origin = "lsoa", facility = "practice", count = "patients")

# Fit the travel scale sigma and the outside weight v0 to the registrations
clm <- spax(d, spec_clm(), observed = flows)
observed: 2,290 counts from 1 origin outside the data or left out by it are dropped; 5 counts at 1 facility outside the data are not fitted (outside = "known" uses them as outside counts)
coef(clm)
     sigma         v0 
4.59099725 0.02733454

spax() reports that it drops the 2,290 registrations of the Isles of Scilly area, and does not fit the 5 mainland residents registered at the Scilly practice, because the example keeps mainland Cornwall only.

The travel scale σ is about 4.6 minutes, so a practice 9 minutes away, about twice σ, pulls only about 15% as strongly as one of the same size next door. Registration is very local. The outside weight v0 acts like a practice of 0.03 GP FTE next door to every area. With it the model places 0.54% of registered residents with practices outside mainland Cornwall, against 0.91% observed. This fit uses only the counts at mainland practices. Where do residents register? shows how to give it each area’s known outside count too.

Learn more

The guides follow one story on the Cornwall data, and each answers one question. Read them on the package website. In R, vignette("<name>", package = "spax") opens one if your installation built the guides. If it finds nothing, use the website.

Where do residents register? Fitting an allocation model "allocation-workflow"

Contributing and license

Report reproducible issues or discuss larger changes on the project repository. Package code uses the MIT license; see LICENSE. The bundled Cornwall GP example data are openly licensed third-party material (Open Government Licence v3.0 and Creative Commons Attribution), which the MIT license does not cover. The installed notice file, system.file("COPYRIGHTS", package = "spax") (source inst/COPYRIGHTS), lists each source and its required attribution.
